correctness.rationale: For width at most one and a nonempty path set, exactly one string occurs at each level and is eventually enumerated, yielding a uniform exact selector. For width at most two, the recursion-theorem construction branches at fresh levels, extends a provisional child while waiting for the candidate output, and then continues the opposite bit. Every level has at most two nodes, every abandoned side branch is finite, and the construction preserves a unique infinite path even if a simulated computation stalls. If the candidate is total on the promised class, it disagrees at infinitely many fresh coordinates, contradicting eventual agreement.

value.rationale: The singleton-path promise removes multiplicity of infinite branches as an explanation for nonuniformity. The exact contrast between width one (uniform exact selection) and width two (no one-program finite-error selector) isolates the smallest width at which this uniformity obstruction appears. The claim is a self-contained boundary theorem rather than a finite experimental observation.
